---
title: "5 dsDNA Quantification and fmol Calculation"
---

**Approximate time:** 30 minutes

## Equipment and assay

The reference workflow used the Quantus® fluorometer with QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent. A validated alternative fluorometer could be used; record the instrument and calibration used.

**Instrument used**  
<input class="protocol-input" data-field-id="quant-instrument" placeholder="e.g. Quantus / DIY-QuantiFluorONE">

## Using the DIY-QuantiFluorONE dsDNA Fluorometer

The DIY-QuantiFluorONE dsDNA Fluorometer can be used for fluorometric
quantification of the purified PCR products before library preparation.

The instrument reports the concentration of the original DNA sample in
ng/µL. The assay uses 1 µL sample or standard together with 200 µL
QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent.

### Front-panel controls

![QuantiFluorONE front-panel controls for firmware QF1-1.0.0-rc2.](figures/qfo_getting_started_menu_navigation.jpeg)

The firmware defines the controls as follows:

| Physical control | Firmware name | Main measurement-screen function | Menu or dialog function |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upper-left button | `SELECT` | Open the SELECT menu | Open, confirm, load, or save the highlighted action |
| Upper-right button | `START` | Measure and store the reagent blank | Measure a calibration blank or the next blank in the ten-blank study |
| A button | `A` | Measure the selected sample; one cycle contains three sensor readings | Measure the selected high standard during two-point calibration |
| B button | `B` | Cycle Live → Details → RAW → Live | Back or cancel |
| D-pad UP/DOWN | `UP/DOWN` | Select the sample ID | Select a menu item or standard concentration |
| D-pad RIGHT | `RIGHT` | Open or leave the RAW screen | Not used for menu selection |
| D-pad LEFT | `LEFT` | Change RAW page | Change calibration-result or calibration-status page |
| On/Off switch | power | Turn the instrument on or off | — |
| Reset access opening | reset | Restart the PyBadge | Used for normal reset, slow-double-click safe mode, or fast-double-click UF2 bootloader mode |
| USB Micro port | USB | Power, charging, programming, and file access | — |

The last line of the display shows context-sensitive button hints.
These hints take priority whenever a calibration or confirmation dialog is open.

### Quick two-point calibration

- [ ] Allow the QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA standard and reagent to reach room temperature before use.
- [ ] Switch on the DIY-QuantiFluorONE and allow approximately **20 min warm-up time** before the first quantitative measurement.
- [ ] During warm-up, prepare the reagent blank and the high calibration standard in compatible 0.5 mL tubes.
- [ ] Prepare the blank using **200 µL QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent**.
- [ ] Prepare the high standard using **200 µL QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent + 1 µL QuantiFluor® ONE Lambda DNA stock (400 ng/µL)** and mix thoroughly without introducing bubbles.
- [ ] Open the `SELECT` menu and select the **2-PT calibration** workflow.
- [ ] Insert the blank tube and press `START` to measure the calibration blank.
- [ ] Remove the blank and keep it protected from light.
- [ ] Insert the prepared high-standard tube.
- [ ] Confirm the standard step with `SELECT`.
- [ ] Press `A` to measure the high standard.
- [ ] Press `SELECT` to save the two-point calibration.
- [ ] Press `B` to return to the measurement screen.

Typical values observed for the validated instrument configuration are:

- calibration slope: approximately **114.5 ± 0.5**;
- raw reagent blank: approximately **6500–8500 counts**;
- 400 ng/µL standard: approximately **45,800 ± 500 RFU**.

These values are operational reference values rather than independent
acceptance limits. A fresh reagent blank should be measured whenever the
measurement session or optical/reagent conditions have changed.

### Sample measurement

For each PCR product:

- [ ] Select the required sample ID using the D-pad `UP/DOWN` buttons.
- [ ] Prepare **200 µL QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent + 1 µL sample**.
- [ ] Mix thoroughly without introducing visible bubbles.
- [ ] Insert the tube into the instrument.
- [ ] Press `A` to measure the sample.
- [ ] Record the reported concentration together with the sample ID.
- [ ] Retain the measurement record together with the corresponding amplicon length used for the molar conversion.

### Conversion from DNA concentration to fmol

The amount of DNA in femtomoles depends on the length of the PCR product.

For double-stranded DNA, using an average molar mass of approximately

$$
660\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}\,bp^{-1}},
$$

the molecular mass of an amplicon of length \(L\) is approximately

$$
M = 660L\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}.
$$

For a DNA concentration \(c\) in ng/µL and a volume \(V\) in µL:

$$
n_{\mathrm{fmol}}
=
\frac{
c\,V\,10^6
}{
660L
}.
$$

where:

- \(n_{\mathrm{fmol}}\) = amount of DNA in fmol;
- \(c\) = measured DNA concentration in ng/µL;
- \(V\) = DNA volume in µL;
- \(L\) = representative amplicon length in bp.

The DNA volume required for a selected molar amount is therefore:

$$
V
=
\frac{
n_{\mathrm{fmol}}\,660L
}{
10^6c
}.
$$

For a target of **100 fmol**, the corresponding DNA mass is:

$$
m_{100}
=
0.066L\ \mathrm{ng}.
$$

Examples:

| Amplicon length | DNA mass for 100 fmol | Concentration equivalent when \(V=1\) µL |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 245 bp | 16.17 ng | 16.17 ng/µL |
| 320 bp | 21.12 ng | 21.12 ng/µL |
| 726 bp | 47.92 ng | 47.92 ng/µL |
| 1000 bp | 66.00 ng | 66.00 ng/µL |
| 2000 bp | 132.00 ng | 132.00 ng/µL |

Thus, the former 726-bp example

$$
48\ \mathrm{ng}
\approx
100\ \mathrm{fmol}
$$

is only valid for a fragment close to 726 bp and must not be used as a
general conversion factor for SHARK-Seq products.

### Open-validation uncertainty estimate

As part of the open-validation concept, an approximate upper-bound
uncertainty can be estimated from the observed variation of the raw
reagent blank between measurement sessions.

For the validated instrument configuration, a calibration slope of
approximately

$$
b = 114.7 \pm 0.5\ \mathrm{RFU\,(ng/\mu L)^{-1}}
$$

was observed. Historical raw blank values were approximately
6000–9000 counts.

Using half of this observed range as a conservative estimate,

$$
\Delta B \approx \pm1500\ \mathrm{counts},
$$

the corresponding concentration deviation is

$$
\Delta c
=
\frac{\Delta B}{b}
\approx
\frac{1500}{114.7}
\approx
\pm13.1\ \mathrm{ng/\mu L}.
$$

For a **726-bp dsDNA amplicon** and a DNA volume of \(1\ \mu L\),

$$
\Delta n_{\mathrm{fmol}}
=
\frac{
\Delta c\,10^6
}{
660 \times 726
}
\approx
\pm27\ \mathrm{fmol}.
$$

Thus, for a 726-bp amplicon, the historical session-to-session blank
variation corresponds to a conservative estimated uncertainty of
approximately **±25–30 fmol**.

This value is not a universal uncertainty of the instrument. It is an
openly documented upper-bound estimate for the stated amplicon length
and observed blank range. The corresponding molar uncertainty changes
with amplicon length. A current reagent blank and 400 ng/uL standard 
should therefore always be measured for quantitative work.

## Measurement

- [ ] Prepare / measure a fresh reagent blank according to the active fluorometer procedure.
- [ ] Confirm calibration is valid for the expected concentration range.
- [ ] Add 200 µL QuantiFluor® ONE dsDNA reagent to a clean 0.5 mL clear tube.
- [ ] Add 1 µL unknown sample unless the active instrument protocol specifies another sample volume.
- [ ] Mix consistently and protect from light.
- [ ] Measure and record the dsDNA concentration in ng/µL.

## Convert ng to fmol using the **actual amplicon length**

For dsDNA using approximately 660 g mol⁻¹ per base pair:

$$
\mathrm{fmol}=\frac{c\,[\mathrm{ng/\mu L}]\times V\,[\mathrm{\mu L}]\times10^6}{660\times L\,[\mathrm{bp}]}
$$

For a target molar amount:

$$
V\,[\mathrm{\mu L}]=\frac{n\,[\mathrm{fmol}]\times660\times L\,[\mathrm{bp}]}{10^6\times c\,[\mathrm{ng/\mu L}]}
$$

### Practical target

The WAMBAnet end-prep step specifies approximately **100–200 fmol** of amplicon DNA. A useful mid-range planning value is **150 fmol**, but the workshop lead should confirm the actual target for the current library-preparation kit.

| Example length | DNA mass for 100 fmol | DNA mass for 150 fmol | DNA mass for 200 fmol |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 245 bp | 16.2 ng | 24.3 ng | 32.3 ng |
| 320 bp | 21.1 ng | 31.7 ng | 42.2 ng |
| 726 bp (old WAMBAnet COI example) | 47.9 ng | 71.9 ng | 95.8 ng |
| 2000 bp | 132 ng | 198 ng | 264 ng |

::: {.callout-important}
The old WAMBAnet shortcut “100 fmol ≈ 48 ng” applied only to an approximately 726 bp COI product. SHARK-Seq uses different fragment lengths, so the **general formula must be used**.
:::
